llm.reply:
KRAS encodes a small GTPase, and its gene product functions as a molecular switch that controls downstream growth signaling when mutated [1].

## Gene Identity

The gene symbol is KRAS [1], also referred to by the gene name KRAS [5] and by the literature entity name Kras [6].

## Molecular Function

KRAS is described as a Kirsten ras oncogene homolog encoding a protein that belongs to the small GTPase superfamily, with a single amino acid substitution able to cause an activating mutation whose transforming protein is implicated in several cancers including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, pancreatic ductal carcinoma, and colorectal carcinoma [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"][11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"].

## Disease Relevance

Constitutively activated KRAS acts as a molecular switch that persistently stimulates downstream signaling pathways governing cell proliferation and survival, driving tumorigenesis in colorectal cancer, where mutations occur in roughly 40% of cases [26: "its mutations result in constitutive activation of the KRAS protein, which acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival, thereby leading to tumorigenesis"].

The KRAS gene product is a member of the small GTPase superfamily, and its normal role as a molecular switch becomes constitutively active when mutated, driving downstream proliferative signaling in cancer [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"][26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways"].

## Gene identity

The gene is officially named KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS.
[4]
Its symbol is KRAS.
[1]
Its name is KRAS.
[5]
In the literature it is also referred to as Kras.
[6]

## Gene function and disease role

The KRAS gene is a Kirsten ras oncogene homolog whose product is implicated in malignancies including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma, with alternative splicing producing two C-terminal isoforms [11: "The transforming protein that results is implicated in various malignancies, including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma"][11: "Alternative splicing leads to variants encoding two isoforms that differ in the C-terminal region"]. A single amino acid substitution can convert the protein into an activating, transforming oncoprotein [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"]. Reviews describe KRAS as the most frequently mutated oncogene in cancer and note that this GTPase target was long considered undruggable before recent inhibitor development [27: "As the most frequently mutated oncogene, Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homologue (KRAS) has attracted substantial attention"][9]. In colorectal cancer specifically, KRAS mutations occur in roughly 40% of cases and are associated with a poor prognosis [26: "with mutations in approximately 40% of all CRC cases"][26: "Patients whose CRC harbors KRAS mutations have a dismal prognosis"]. Oncogenic KRAS has also been shown to reprogram tumor-associated fibroblasts to promote angiogenesis and colorectal cancer progression [14][28: "KRAS* transforms the phenotype of carcinoma-associated fibroblasts (CAF) into lipid-laden CAFs, promoting angiogenesis and tumor progression"]. In pancreatic cancer, KRAS is mutated in up to 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas, most commonly at codon 12 [18][29: "The Kirsten rat sarcoma virus (KRAS) oncogene is mutated in up to 90% of all pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDACs)"].

## Sequence variants recorded

ClinVar records for this gene include NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.458ATG[1] (p.Asp154del).

## Therapeutic targeting efforts

Because KRAS's GTPase activity underlies oncogenic signaling, considerable effort has gone into drugging it, from small-molecule inhibitors of the G12C allele to newer pan-KRAS degrader approaches [22][30: "we designed a heterobifunctional small molecule that potently degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"]. This work is reflected in publications with PMIDs 34742312, 34776511, 37768068, 38686056, and 39298590, as well as clinical trials such as Sorafenib in Combination With Irinotecan in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients With KRAS Mutated Tumors, PREMIUM Observational Study, A Trial of mFOLFIRI With MEK162 in Patients With Advanced RAS (HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS) Positive Metastatic Colorectal Cancers, Frequency of EGFR and KRAS Mutations and Clinical-prognostic Correlation in Brazilian Lung Cancer Patients, and A Phase 1/2, Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, PK, and Efficacy of Sotorasib (AMG 510) in Subjects With Solid Tumors With a Specific KRAS Mutation (CodeBreaK 100).
[8][13][17][21][25][7][12][16][20][24]
